prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies distribution circuits via transformer/feeder bays. Automation boundary covers bay monitoring/control, station coordination and external interfaces; primary equipment, protection and field wiring stay under approved designs/limits. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) does bay sequencing, status evaluation, permissives/interlocks for automated operations; produces Bay Status Digest; requests breaker operations from Breaker Control Unit only when mode/permissives allow. North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller automate their station portions. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) gives local protection independent of supervisory availability using approved setting group; produces Relay Diagnostic Note. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized operations and enforces authoritative local interlocks. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) is the operator interface, presents indications and coordinates supervision; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; no protective functions. Station Gateway bounds authorized external/remote comms. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) distributes time; produces Clock Drift Snapshot when offset meets reporting condition; holdover degrades on reference loss. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard) is the authoritative repository of time-stamped event evidence, kept in received form; each record has source identity, event time, receipt time and quality indications. Engineering Workstation keeps revision-controlled configuration (engineering-only access); produces Settings Review Receipt. Maintenance Remote Terminal: approved maintenance access only. Station DC System supplies control power; loss can interrupt visibility/timing. Actors: Control Room Operator directs operation, may suspend work, authorizes return to automated operation after evaluating field reports. Switching Desk Coordinator confirms switching/clearance before work and handback before return to service. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) develops setting changes against approved study and records approval; a second qualified reviewer checks independently. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) does inspections, maintenance, switching support and setting transfer after authorization; verifies equipment identity; sends Breaker Inspection Tag (breaker condition, inspection time). Substation Supervisor confirms work fits conditions/procedures. Requirements: protection independent of bay control; local control precedence; remote commands subject to permissions/interlocks; unique revision ID; no approval from copied values; coordination checks; pre-deployment model/firmware check; approved work window; post-install comparison/functional check; discrepancies halt release. Stale data must be confirmed. Field: pre-entry review, arrival/departure logged, boundaries set, no reliance on screens alone; field/control-room discrepancy treated as unsafe; maintain comms, stop work on comms loss; automation doesn't replace

New part:
S102: The archive preserves original event ordering and marks records whose time quality or sequence continuity is uncertain.
S103: The Satellite Time Receiver supports station time alignment, and loss of its reference is treated as a condition affecting interpretation rather than a reason to discard evidence.
S104: Events with corrected or estimated times remain distinguishable from records with valid time quality.
S105: The Sequence Event Archive retains configuration and access history associated with archive administration.
S106: The Station Supervisory Control System presents current operating indications separately from the long-term evidence held by the archive.
S107: The Control Room Operator reviews archived event sequences to establish the order of alarms, status changes, and operator actions.
S108: The Protection Relay Engineer compares event times and relay indications during disturbance analysis.
S109: The Protection Relay Engineer uses the Relay Diagnostic Note during fault analysis.
S110: The Engineering Workstation provides approved tools for searching, filtering, and exporting event records.
S111: Review queries should be bounded by station, equipment identifier, and time interval to keep results reproducible.
S112: Exported evidence retains original timestamps and quality flags, and any derived ordering is identified as an engineering interpretation.
S113: Engineering conclusions are recorded separately from the preserved source evidence.
S114: Access to archive functions is limited to authorized roles, and administrative changes are auditable.
S115: The archive retains records under the station records schedule and applicable utility retention requirements.
S116: Records selected for an investigation are protected from routine deletion until the hold is released by the responsible authority.
S117: Archive health is checked for storage capacity, ingestion continuity, and recoverability.
S118: Recovery testing verifies that retained records remain readable and that timestamps and quality indications survive restoration.
S119: The station preserves an additional protected copy of essential event evidence in accordance with approved backup procedures.
S120: The Station DC System produces a Battery Load Test Record for retention with station engineering records.
S121: Juniper timestamps locally generated state changes for later correlation.
S122: After the Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback, evidence from the completed work remains available for authorized engineering review.
S123: The Switching Desk Coordinator is known operationally as Keystone.
S124: The Switching Desk Coordinator maintains the station-wide switching plan and coordinates work across the two bay boundaries.
S125: The Control Room Operator submits switching requests with the affected equipment, intended state changes, and requested timing.
S126: The Switching Desk Coordinator checks each request for conflicts with active clearances and other approved work.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
